Emily / Ava / Laura —

Thanks for the note. I reviewed Sunnyside's template language and sketched conservative redlines that balance audit rights with our operational constraints. High-level:

- SOC 2: we'll provide the latest Type II report for the period Jan 1 2026 — Dec 31 2026. Full report access via our secure portal (non-disclosable copy) and a summary table in the Order Form.

- Pen Test / Audit Rights: propose the following bullets for the Assurance Exhibit (short form):
  * Customer may perform one third-party penetration test per 12-month period (no more than once in rolling 12 months), with at least 30 days prior written notice;
  * Tests must be scoped to a non-production staging environment unless otherwise expressly agreed in writing;
  * Customer testers shall not exploit findings actively in production or exfiltrate PII; any high/critical findings must be coordinated through Redwood's security ops playbook;
  * Redwood will provide a one-time set of logs/artifacts related to the scope within 10 business days of request; for sampled or recurring evidence we propose a weekly snapshot cadence for six weeks post-onboarding, then monthly thereafter (we can refine based on the customer's needs).

- Redaction & Confidentiality: added a short process for redaction requests and an NDA-preserved handling clause.

I've attached a tracked-changes doc (Sunnyside_OrderForm_redlines_v1.docx). These are intentionally conservative; happy to tighten the notice or expand staging access if we get clear guardrails from Sunnyside about their testers and scope.

Laura — can you confirm the feasibility of the 10-business-day artifact turnaround and the proposed snapshot cadence? If 10 days is tight, propose a fallback of 15 business days.

Emily — please let us know any must-have language and whether your legal team will accept staging-only by default. If not, we'll discuss compensating controls (on-call window, scheduled maintenance blackout, monitored session).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik — quick operational notes from Security Ops: 

- 10 business days to produce a one-time artifact set is doable if the scope is limited (list of specific endpoints, log ranges, and timeframe). If the request is broad ("all logs for six months"), we'll need 15 business days plus additional approvals.
- Weekly snapshots for the first six weeks is fine as an onboarding pattern; afterwards monthly is fine but we'll include an exception process for audit-triggered sampling.
- Staging access: we recommend staging-by-default. If Sunnyside requires production testing, we require an agreed runbook: scheduled window, monitored session with Redwood on-call, and explicit approval of test cases.

I'll add a short 'evidence playbook' annex to the redlines before we hand back to Emily.
